diagnostic_evidence.quote:
When the 2D space is considered,
there exists a constant $C$ such that for all $\bmf{v}\in \bmf{H}^2$,
the following inequalities hold:

issues.failure_explanation: The third inequality of (2.10) asserts \|v\|_{L^\infty} \le C(\|v\|_{L^2}^2 + \|\Delta v\|_{L^2}^2)^{1/2} for every v \in H^2. This is false on any 2D domain: harmonic functions v_n = Re(z^n) satisfy \Delta v_n = 0 with \|v_n\|_{L^\infty} = O(1) (attained on \partial\Omega) while \|v_n\|_{L^2} = O(n^{-1/2}) \to 0, so no such uniform C exists. The bound is valid for v \in H^2 \cap H_0^1 (elliptic regularity \|v\|_{H^2} \le C\|\Delta v\|_{L^2} + C\|v\|_{L^2}, then H^2 \hookrightarrow L^\infty), and every later application (error function \xi, iteration differences w^l, auxiliary solutions) is to functions vanishing on \partial\Omega, but as stated the zero-trace hypothesis is missing.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restrict the third (and similarly the fourth) inequality of (2.10) to v \in H^2 \cap H_0^1, which covers every application in the paper.
issues.overall_effect: One displayed inequality of (2.10) is incorrect as stated; no lemma, proposition, or theorem is damaged because all of its uses are for functions with zero trace.
issues.title: The L^infinity Sobolev inequality is claimed for all H^2 functions but is false without a boundary condition
issues.why_classification: Adding the standard zero-trace condition repairs the display in one line and leaves every result, estimate, and rate unchanged.

failure_location.quote:
Assume the regularity condition \eqref{regularity-condition} to be satisfied.
For a sufficiently small $ \tau $, there holds
$$ \lim_{l \rightarrow \infty} \|\tilde{\bmf{m}}^{l+1}-\tilde{\bmf{m}}^l\|_{\bmf{H}^2} \rightarrow 0.$$

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the standard induction: assume \|\tilde m^l\|_{H^3} \le R, apply the same energy estimates to (3.7) for \tilde m^{l+1} to obtain \|\tilde m^{l+1}\|_{H^3} \le R for R = 2(\|\tilde m\|_{H^3}+1) and \tau sufficiently small; the displayed contraction estimates then go through verbatim.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem-con is established only conditionally on unstated uniform iterate bounds; Theorem thm-error, whose proof invokes Lemma lem-con for the convergence \tilde m^l \to m, inherits the gap.
issues.title: Contraction proof for the fixed-point iteration absorbs uniform bounds on the iterates that are never established
issues.why_classification: The fix is a contained but nontrivial additional argument (an induction with energy estimates parallel to those already written); the statement, its role, and all rates survive unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: With \Phi frozen at \Phi(Q) on each element, the appendix's own computation gives b_h(\Phi(Q);u,I_h^*v) = -\sum_K S_K[(\Phi(Q)\times u_x)\cdot v_x + (\Phi(Q)\times u_y)\cdot v_y] (up to the factor in (triangle_area)), which is exactly skew-symmetric in (u,v) since (\Phi\times a)\cdot b = -(\Phi\times b)\cdot a. Hence b_h(\Phi;u,I_h^*v) - b_h(\Phi;v,I_h^*u) = 2b_h(\Phi;u,I_h^*v) + O(h\|u\|_1\|v\|_1), which is O(\|u\|_1\|v\|_1) in general, not O(h): e.g. \Phi = e_1 with u,v \in S_h satisfying \nabla u = e_2, \nabla v = e_3 on a fixed patch of elements gives a difference equal to a nonzero multiple of the patch area, independent of h. So (Ah-relation) and (bh-relation) are false as stated. The appendix proof cannot save them: the E_1-E_5 analysis bounds the consistency b(\Phi;\tilde m-\tilde m_h,v_h) - b_h(\Phi;\tilde m-\tilde m_h,I_h^*v_h) for \tilde m \in H^2, and since the continuous form b is exactly antisymmetric, the triangle-inequality route yields only an O(1) antisymmetry defect of b_h on S_h \times S_h. Proposition pro2's H^1 sub-proof applies the false bound in the step bounded as 'C h \|\xi\|_{H^1} \|\partial_t\xi\|_{H^1}' (mis-citing Lemma lem-Ah); with the true O(1) bound, the inverse-inequality step produces a factor h^{-1} and that argument collapses.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete Lemma lem-Ah1 and the v_h = \partial_t\xi asymmetry argument in pro2; instead obtain \|\xi\|_{H^1} \le C h directly from the valid estimate \|\xi\|_{L^2} \le C h^2 via the inverse inequality \|\xi\|_{H^1} \le C h^{-1}\|\xi\|_{L^2} on the quasi-uniform mesh, then conclude with (R_h_p) as before.
issues.overall_effect: Lemma lem-Ah1 must be abandoned (no O(h) near-symmetry of A_h exists); the H^1 half of Proposition pro2's proof is invalid as written, although pro2's stated H^1 rate, and hence Theorem thm-error's rates, survive by a different one-line argument.
issues.title: The O(h) near-symmetry of A_h claimed in Lemma lem-Ah1 is false: the cross-product form b_h is O(1)-skew-symmetric
issues.why_classification: Although the stated lemma is false, its only application has a short, routine bypass (one inverse-inequality line from the valid L^2 estimate) that preserves the advertised L^2/H^1 rates and every downstream claim; no new lemma or weakened statement is required.

Choose $\bmf{\Phi} = \tilde{\bmf{m}}_h^l$, and
the FVEM scheme \eqref{auxiliary} is equivalent to the FVEM scheme \eqref{equ:LL-semi-discretized1},

issues.failure_explanation: The splitting m - m_h = (m - \tilde m^l) + (\tilde m^l - \tilde m_h^l) + (\tilde m_h^l - m_h) is closed by three unsupported assertions. (i) Lemma lem-con only shows that the backward-Euler iterates of (3.7) at fixed \tau = T_2 - T_1 form a convergent (Cauchy) sequence; their limit solves the \tau-discrete implicit problem, not the exact solution m of the PDE, so 'lim \|m - \tilde m^l\| = 0' uses the lemma outside its established content (an O(\tau) time discrepancy remains). (ii) Proposition pro2 compares the time-continuous auxiliary problem (3.1) with the semi-discrete scheme (3.8); applying it to the middle term requires \tilde m^l to solve (3.1) with \Phi = \tilde m^{l-1}, i.e. the continuous iteration (3.6), whose convergence and uniformity (including the \|\nabla\tilde m^{l-1}\|_{L^\infty}-dependence of pro2's constant) are never proved — only the \tau-discrete variant is treated. (iii) 'Choose \Phi = \tilde m_h^l, then (3.8) is equivalent to (2.8) in the limit' presupposes convergence of a discrete fixed-point iteration \tilde m_h^l \to m_h that is never established: the difference equation for \tilde m_h^l - m_h contains b_h(\Phi - m_h; \cdot, \cdot) with \Phi - m_h = (\tilde m^{l-1} - m) + (m - m_h), i.e. the unknown error itself, and the required coupled stability/Gronwall argument is absent.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Prove contraction of the continuous-in-time iteration (3.6) on a short time interval with uniform bounds in X (paralleling Appendix A), apply Proposition pro2 with \Phi = \tilde m^{l-1} to the middle term, and add a discrete stability estimate of (3.8) with respect to \Phi closed jointly with the continuous error by a Gronwall argument.
issues.overall_effect: All three terms of the splitting in the proof of the paper's central error estimate (L^2 order h^2, H^1 order h) are uncontrolled as written; the statement of Theorem thm-error itself is the expected standard result.
issues.title: Proof of the main error theorem closes the iteration splitting with convergence claims the cited lemma does not provide
issues.why_classification: The repair needs one or two contained new lemmas proved with techniques already in the paper and leaves the statement, rates, and scope intact; no new global architecture or loss of content.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Assume that the boundary condition \eqref{equ:general-boundary-condtion} holds true and the discrete magnetization $\bmf{m}_h$ satisfies $|\bmf{m}_h| = 1$ in a point-wise sense.

issues.failure_explanation: Testing (3.18) with v_h = \partial_t m_h leaves the terms (m_h \times \partial_t m_h, I_h^*\partial_t m_h), \epsilon(|\nabla m_h|^2 m_h, I_h^*\partial_t m_h), and ((m_h\cdot\hat f)m_h, I_h^*\partial_t m_h), which the proof silently drops as if the lumped inner product (\cdot, I_h^*\cdot) preserved the pointwise orthogonality identities. It does not: (m_h \times \partial_t m_h, I_h^*\partial_t m_h) = \sum_i \partial_t m_h(P_i) \cdot \int_{V_i} m_h \times \partial_t m_h dx is generically nonzero, and even granting m_h \cdot \partial_t m_h = 0 pointwise, m_h \cdot \partial_t m_h(P_i) = -m_h \cdot (\partial_t m_h - \partial_t m_h(P_i)) = O(h)|\nabla \partial_t m_h|, so the two right-side terms do not vanish either; likewise d_t(\hat F(m_h),1) = -(\hat f(m_h), \partial_t m_h) is the non-lumped inner product, not the lumped one appearing in the displayed identity for d_t F[m_h]. Moreover the hypothesis '|m_h| = 1 pointwise' cannot hold for a nonconstant piecewise-linear m_h \in S_h (a piecewise affine map into S^2 is constant), so the proposition is vacuous as stated; under the intended nodal condition |m_h(P_i)| = 1 the residuals persist, with sizes O(h\|\partial_t m_h\|^2) (absorbable for small h) and O(h\|\partial_t m_h\|) (a forcing after Young's inequality), so the clean decay d_t F[m_h] \le 0 is not established.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the proposition with the nodal unit-length assumption and prove the perturbed law d_t F[m_h] \le -c\|\partial_t m_h\|^2 + C h^2 for sufficiently small h by estimating each lumping residual (the cross term, the |\nabla m_h|^2 m_h term, the (m_h\cdot\hat f)m_h term, and the consistency error in d_t(\hat F,1)); or modify the discrete form/energy so that the orthogonality identities hold exactly.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition energy-dissipation — the paper's only discrete energy result, advertised in the abstract ('depict the discretized energy dissipation') and underlying the energy-decay narrative of Sections 4.3 and 4.5 — is unproved as stated; only a perturbed dissipation law survives.
issues.title: Discrete energy law proof discards non-vanishing mass-lumping residuals; the pointwise |m_h| = 1 hypothesis is impossible in the P1 space
issues.why_classification: The clean monotone law must be weakened by explicit consistency terms (or the scheme/energy modified) — a limited weakening leaving a recognizably comparable dissipation statement; no other labelled formal result depends on it.

issues.failure_explanation: In the \Delta t = \Delta x^2 block the spatial mesh is doubled between consecutive rows, so each 'order' entry equals log_2 of the ratio of the errors in successive rows. Computing from the table's own error values for the last two rows gives L^\infty orders log_2(4.95e-3/2.19e-3) \approx 1.18 and log_2(2.19e-3/1.23e-4) \approx 4.16 (tabulated 2.01 and 2.01), L^2 orders \approx 1.41 and \approx 0.91 (tabulated 2.41 and 2.19), and H^1 orders \approx 0.60 and \approx 0.42 (tabulated 1.13 and 1.00). Hence the displayed errors in these rows do not support the reported orders; by contrast every row of Table 5 and the first refinement row of Table 7 are internally consistent. Either the error values or the order values are misprinted, and the correct values cannot be uniquely determined from the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the misprinted entries in the last two rows of Table 7 so that the error columns and the order columns agree.
issues.overall_effect: Part of the numerical evidence for second-order spatial convergence at \alpha = 0.05 is self-contradictory; the claimed spatial rates remain supported by Table 5 and by the first refinement row of Table 7, and the theory is unaffected.
issues.title: Last two refinement rows of Table 7 report convergence orders inconsistent with the tabulated errors
issues.why_classification: A local data correction with no impact on any theoretical claim; the advertised convergence behavior is corroborated by the remaining consistent rows and tables.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose presents the experiment as finite-time blow-up from a smooth initialization, and the analysis section stresses that the theory applies only to smooth solutions away from blow-up. But with A = (1-2|x|^2)^4 and the branch switch at |x| = 0.5, the inner branch has, as |x| \to 0.5^-, A \to (1-2\cdot 0.25)^4 = 1/16 \ne 0 and m_0 \to (32x/65, 32y/65, -63/65), while the outer branch is (0,0,-1)^T: m_0 jumps across the circle |x| = 0.5, and the inherited fixed Dirichlet boundary data jump at (\pm 0.5, 0) and (0, \pm 0.5). The same shifted profile (A = (1-2|x-x_0|^2)^4, switch at |x-x_0| = 0.5) is used in the micromagnetics example of Section 4.5. Continuity would require A \to 0 at the interface (e.g. A = (1-2|x|)^4) or moving the switch to |x| = 1/\sqrt{2}; since two distinct repairs are possible, this is not a pure typo. The stated data are not even continuous, let alone smooth.

failure_location.quote: With a smooth initialization, the solution of the LL equation would blow up in a finite-time evolution.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Modify the profile so that A vanishes on the interface circle (e.g. A = (1-2|x|)^4 for the switch at |x| = 0.5), restoring continuity of the initial data and of the boundary condition.
issues.overall_effect: The two blow-up experiments (Sections 4.4 and 4.5) are run with discontinuous initial/boundary data while being described as blow-up from smooth initializations; no theoretical result is affected.
issues.title: Blow-up initial data are discontinuous across |x| = 0.5 although the initialization is claimed to be smooth
issues.why_classification: A local correction to the data of two numerical examples; all theoretical claims and the qualitative blow-up conclusions are unaffected.

issues.failure_explanation: The chain of equalities replaces \int_{\overline{M_iQM_{i+2}}} \Phi \times \partial_\nu \tilde m_h dS by (\Phi \times \partial_\nu \tilde m_h(Q)) times edge-length differences, which is valid only if \Phi is constant on the dual edges. For a general \Phi \in X the constant-\Phi part vanishes (since (\Phi(Q) \times u_x)\cdot u_x + (\Phi(Q) \times u_y)\cdot u_y = 0) but the remainder does not: b_h(\Phi; u, I_h^*u) = O(h\|u\|_{H^1}^2), not 0 (the self-case \Phi = u \in S_h is likewise nonzero in general). Hence (bh_coe) is false as an equality, and the concluding coercivity chain of app:lem-Ah ('A_h(\Phi;\tilde m_h,I_h^*\tilde m_h) = a_h + b_h \ge C\|\tilde m_h\|_{H^1}^2') requires absorbing the additional Ch\|\tilde m_h\|_{H^1}^2 into the coercive a_h term.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate (bh_coe) as |b_h(\Phi; u, I_h^*u)| \le C h \|u\|_{H^1}^2 (freeze \Phi at \Phi(Q) and estimate the remainder), and add the one-line absorption into a_h's coercivity in the proof of Lemma lem-Ah.
issues.overall_effect: The intermediate claim (bh_coe) is false as stated; the parent result Lemma lem-Ah remains true (its hypothesis of sufficiently small h already allows absorbing the O(h) perturbation), so Proposition pro2 and Theorem thm-error, which only use the coercivity and boundedness, are not damaged.
issues.title: The claim b_h(Phi; m_h, I_h^* m_h) = 0 is false for variable Phi; the proof treats Phi as constant inside the edge integrals
issues.why_classification: The false equality is repaired by a standard O(h) perturbation bound and a one-line absorption; every substantive claim (coercivity, error estimates) is preserved.
